content.text:
Recommend a persistent shared `ContentChange` wrapper that briefly fades in updated results when the committed period changes. Keep controls outside it. This preserves DOM identity, focus, disclosure state and exact amounts while avoiding simultaneous old/new accessible content. Current flow is already suitable: `PeriodSelector` builds native links; server loads supply the validated `ReportingPeriod`; summaries and rankings retain committed content during same-page navigation; `aria-busy` lives on the page. Animate only after those loaded props change. Do not introduce separate selected-period or loading state. Usage sketch: ```svelte
``` Small APIs: ```ts // lib/ui/ContentChange.svelte type Props = { changeKey: string | number; children: Snippet; }; // Extend existing ViewLinks: type ViewLinksAlign = "start" | "end"; type Props = { children: Snippet; label?: string; variant?: ViewLinksVariant; align?: ViewLinksAlign; // default start }; ``` `PeriodSelector` uses ``. Full-width navigation with `justify-content: flex-end` right-aligns links and wrapped lines. For rankings, moving the selector beneath `.ranking-intro` gives it the actual content width; adding alignment while leaving it inside the current narrow heading column would not satisfy “move to the right.” `ContentChange` owns one stable wrapper and its animation lifecycle: skip initial mount; observe `changeKey`; cancel any prior animation; animate wrapper opacity from approximately `0.65` to `1` over roughly 180–220 ms; cancel on disposal. Use a browser-only Svelte effect and Web Animations API, with reduced-motion detection inside that effect. Include reduced-motion changes during an active animation if feasible. No key block, outro, delayed replacement, number interpolation or geometry animation. The component hides cancellation and initial-render policy behind one input; features retain knowledge of what a completed change means. Keep the existing native `data-sveltekit-reset={false}` behavior. The persistent selector remains focusable throughout; preserve scroll and current `aria-current` until data commits. Leave existing loading/error behavior alone. A failed load must still remove prior-scope financial output. Existing `RankingList` entry animations can remain; the wrapper need not remount it or replay all row entry effects. Files: - `frontend/src/lib/ui/ContentChange.svelte` — new presentation behavior. - `frontend/src/lib/ui/{ViewLinks.svelte,types.ts,styles.css,index.ts}` — typed alignment and barrel export. - `frontend/src/PeriodSelector.svelte` — request end alignment. - `frontend/src/{MemberSummary,FunderSummary}.svelte` and `frontend/src/routes/rankings/+page.svelte` — wrap result content; rankings placement. - `frontend/src/lib/ui/{README.md,COMPOSITION.md}` and design-system gallery — contracts/examples. - `frontend/tests/{periods,design-system}.spec.ts` — focused acceptance. Acceptance: - All three consumers end-align the filter at desktop width; 320px wraps without overflow. - Member/funder filters remain after identity tabs, inside Summary, and absent from history. - Delayed navigation keeps one old result, unchanged selected link and scroll; committed navigation presents one new result and triggers animation. - Keyboard activation leaves the filter usable; Back/Forward animate committed period changes. - Reduced motion produces no animation; initial SSR content remains immediately available. - Exact historical decimal, zero, negative, unavailable and mismatch/error tests continue passing. - Gallery verifies animation on key changes without remounting children; fast successive changes cancel prior animation. Alternatives: a keyed Svelte transition is smaller initially but remounts interactive content and can retain duplicate old/new content during outros. A global View Transition integration hides more navigation mechanics but broadens scope to browser snapshots, navigation coordination and page-wide styling. The persistent local wrapper offers the smallest surface that centralizes the behavior across all three consumers.
